summary: Christiane Antoine's unfinished general chemistry note (draft, 19 Jun 2019) compares candidate small-scale coupling work-ups. It retains mixed mg and handwritten g conventions, open solvent-recovery questions and reviewer changes. Observations and quantities are to be checked against the bench records before recommendations are completed.

blocks.p: This note compares candidate small-scale work-ups for coupling trials. It is a working draft and several sections are incomplete; trial observations remain in the bench records.
The aim is to choose one work-up for the scale-up before the next analogue set is started. Nothing here is a final recommendation.

For comparison, work-up A uses saturated sodium bicarbonate and ethyl acetate; work-up B uses water and dichloromethane; work-up C is a direct evaporation with a silica plug. These are candidate protocols, not a record of confirmed outcomes.

blocks.p: Phase separation and solvent demand must be compared using the bench records before a work-up is preferred. Chlorinated solvent requires the appropriate waste stream unless an approved recovery procedure is used.

blocks.p: Transfer reagent charges and isolated masses from the bench sheet with their original units. The typed sheet uses mg; handwritten entries may use g. Keep both visible until the conversion is checked.
Do not treat isolated mass as percentage yield. Calculation requires the limiting reagent and the assigned product structure. Entries awaiting reconciliation remain [TBC].
Solvent volumes and recovery quantities are to be taken from the work-up records. No recovery recommendation is agreed here.

Solvent recovery from the ethyl acetate washes is still undecided. Confirm the equipment and waste-stream arrangements before deciding whether recovery is practical, so the washes may need to go to the waste stream.
Ask facilities to confirm the recovery setup and approved procedure. A bump trap alone does not establish that a mixed solvent can be safely recovered for reuse.
Which work-up goes forward for the scale-up? This is still open.
